workload.description: 128k-token local Zen context at ~32 KiB KV per token (AIPC-class model: 16 layers x 4 KV heads x 128 dim x K+V x fp16) = 4 GiB of KV in 64 blocks of 64 MiB; 6 blocks resident on device, the rest SSD-backed. 96 decode steps of sparse attention: sliding window of 3 blocks (head-2..head), head advances every 8 steps, attention-sink block 0 re-read every 16 steps (block 0 is resident, so sink re-reads are free). Deterministic trace, no RNG.

default.note: AIPC regime: consumer NVMe SSD ~2 GB/s; iGPU attention over one 64 MiB (~512-token) block ~6 ms per decode step — the regime where prefetch I/O can hide under compute.

simulation_model.per_block_completion: A prefetch issued at step j for a block used at step i hides its I/O under the compute of steps j..i-1 (slack = cumulative compute between issue and use); only the residual (io_ns - slack) stalls at the use step. Demand fetches are synchronous: their full I/O stalls the use step.
simulation_model.why_not_global_drain: A global pending-I/O drain model (idle-loop semantics) double-counts in-flight I/O as stall: an I/O that completes during step k's compute is charged to step k even when the block is not needed until step k+n, where it arrives free. The per-block completion model charges residual latency to the consuming step only.
simulation_model.waste_accounting: Wasted prefetch = prefetched bytes never used before eviction PLUS prefetched-but-never-used staging bytes at end of run (unused_staged_bytes). In this trace exactly one block (12) is prefetched at step 88 and never used: 64 MiB, reported honestly in the B rows.

matched_baselines.description: Three policies over the identical trace and identical pool: (A) demand fetch — no prefetch, synchronous SSD reads; (B) speculative — temporal-locality predictor (predict_next, k=3) stages likely blocks ahead of use; (C) next-step oracle — perfect next-step prediction issued one step before use (depth 1).
matched_baselines.claim: Speculative prefetch (temporal-locality predictor, implicit prefetch depth of up to 8 steps) cuts decode wall time 1.13x on a 2 GB/s NVMe SSD and 1.46x on a 500 MB/s SATA SSD vs demand fetch, while total SSD bytes read are identical (7 prefetched vs 6 demand misses + resident sink: +1 wasted block = 64 MiB, honestly reported).

finding_depth_beats_accuracy.observation: The depth-1 oracle — PERFECT next-step prediction — is SLOWER than the imperfect predictor (1701.6 vs 1608.0 ms on 2 GB/s; 2305.6 vs 1657.6 ms on 500 MB/s).
finding_depth_beats_accuracy.explanation: The oracle issues its prefetch one step before use (depth 1). A 134 ms SATA block read cannot hide under one 18 ms (3-block) decode step, so even perfect prediction stalls. The recency predictor issues at window-epoch start (implicit depth up to 8 steps), giving the I/O several steps of compute to hide under. PREFETCH DEPTH dominates hiding; prediction accuracy is secondary in this regime.
finding_depth_beats_accuracy.implication: For engine integration: schedule prefetches as early as residency/locality allows; do not tune the predictor for accuracy at the cost of issue depth.
finding_depth_beats_accuracy.honesty: The depth-1 oracle is therefore NOT a wall-clock upper bound and is labeled 'next-step oracle (perfect prediction, depth 1)', not 'upper bound'.

metric_honesty.simulation: Per-block I/O latencies are configured rates (2 GB/s / 500 MB/s + 50 µs setup), not measured device I/O; decode compute is a configured 6 ms per 64 MiB block per step. Engine integration must replace these with measured Hanzo-hardware rates.
metric_honesty.policy_layer: The access trace is an INPUT: which blocks sparse attention actually reads (and any answer-quality effect) is the engine's job. This PR measures I/O orchestration only.
metric_honesty.answer_quality: NOT measured — no attention path exists at the fabric policy layer. The bounty's answer-quality regression item requires the engine integration and is listed as follow-up.

hypotheses.text: Demand fetch stalls decode whenever an offload-block read exceeds the step's compute (cold head-of-line per step)
hypotheses.expected_failure_mode: if decode compute per block exceeded SSD block latency, demand fetches would hide naturally and prefetch would add nothing
hypotheses.observed: confirmed: 6 demand misses cost 201.6 ms total stall (2 GB/s) / 805.6 ms (500 MB/s)

hypotheses.text: Speculative prefetch issued several steps ahead hides SSD reads under decode compute, cutting wall time with equal-or-plus-minor wasted bytes
hypotheses.expected_failure_mode: if the predictor mispredicted late (issued too close to use), residual stall would appear — exactly what the depth-1 oracle demonstrates
hypotheses.observed: confirmed: wall 1.13x / 1.46x vs demand; total stall 201.6->0.0 ms (2 GB/s), 805.6->49.6 ms (500 MB/s); cost = one wasted 64 MiB prefetch

hypotheses.text: Perfect prediction at depth 1 is insufficient — depth, not accuracy, dominates hiding
hypotheses.expected_failure_mode: if SSD latency were small relative to one step's compute, a depth-1 oracle would fully hide and beat the predictor
hypotheses.observed: confirmed: depth-1 oracle still stalls (93.6 ms total at 2 GB/s; 697.6 ms at 500 MB/s) and is SLOWER than the depth-8 predictor

hypotheses.text: CacheSalt isolation holds at the offload tier: identical block indices under different tenant salts are disjoint keys
hypotheses.expected_failure_mode: a collision in the key mixer would let one tenant read another's staged block

tests.result: cargo test green on windows/amd64, stdlib-only

out_of_scope: sparse attention algorithms: which blocks attention reads is the engine's job (the trace is an input here)
answer-quality regression: no attention path at the fabric policy layer; requires engine integration (bounty item, follow-up)
fine-grained compute/I-O orchestration inside the attention kernel (SolidAttention leg 3 beyond the bounded per-block overlap model)
real device I/O: configured bandwidths and latencies, not measured — Hanzo-hardware rerun is the follow-up
engine integration into hanzo-engine decode loops, host paging, or CUDA/graphs
multi-tenant concurrent serving (single simulated session; CacheSalt keying provided, concurrency policy is engine work)

upstream_figures_are_not_hanzo_expectati.solidattention_paper: authors report up to 3.1x inference speed improvement and ~98% memory-footprint reduction on their AIPC testbed (FAST '26)
upstream_figures_are_not_hanzo_expectati.stance: not reproduced on Hanzo hardware; not treated as Hanzo expectations per the bounty's own caveat. Our fabric-policy figures (1.13x-1.46x decode wall on the deterministic trace) are the only numbers this PR claims.
